question: What two key parts make up the true foundation of nursing?
explanation: You've got this! Nursing is a beautiful mix of scientific facts and the human art of showing genuine care to people. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why do we call nursing a science when we are doing clinical procedures?

options.B: It requires artistic drawing of charts
options.C: It focuses mainly on hospital building design
options.D: It relies on biological principles and evidence

explanation: Spot on! The science part means we use proven medical facts and careful assessments to keep our patients safe. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h1)

question: Who is known worldwide as the founder of modern nursing?
explanation: Wonderful! Florence Nightingale completely changed how nursing was done during the Crimean War by focusing on cleanliness and organized care. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: How has nursing changed from the way it used to be in the early days?

options.A: It shifted away from patient bedside care completely
options.B: It evolved into a rigorous academic and clinical discipline
options.C: It stopped requiring any formal training or school
options.D: It became entirely focused on hospital administration

explanation: Great job! What started as basic home care has grown into a respected, well-taught professional career. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which global organization defines nursing as both independent and collaborative care?
explanation: You're doing great! The International Council of Nurses gives us the worldwide definition of how nurses practice independently and work with others. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: What does it mean when we say a registered nurse has 'autonomous practice'?

options.A: Working completely isolated from other health workers
options.B: Running a hospital without consulting any doctors
options.C: Prescribing any medication without professional oversight
options.D: Making independent nursing judgments within their scope of practice

explanation: That's it! Autonomy means you are trusted to make smart nursing decisions for patient comfort and basic care within your legal limits. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: In the nursing metaparadigm, what do we call the person or group receiving care?
explanation: Keep it up! The 'person' is simply the individual, family, or community that we are caring for. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: How do we define health in nursing?

options.A: A static score given at hospital discharge
options.B: The permanent absence of any medical condition
options.C: The physical strength to lift heavy objects
options.D: A dynamic state of overall well-being

explanation: Spot on! Health isn't just a fixed score; it's a flowing state of physical, mental, and social wellness. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is a nurse acting as when they stand up to protect a patient's rights?
explanation: Wonderful! Being an advocate means you are the voice that protects your patient's safety and best interests. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h5)

question: A nurse sits down to explain food changes to a new diabetic patient. What role is the nurse playing here?
explanation: You got it! Teaching patients how to manage their own health is a core part of being an educator. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which personal trait helps a nurse stay calm during a sudden hospital emergency?
explanation: Exactly! Having emotional stability helps you stay cool-headed and focused when things get intense. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why do professional nurses need to keep learning throughout their whole career?

options.A: Nursing licenses expire every six months automatically
options.B: Patients refuse care from experienced nurses
options.C: Hospital management requires yearly written exams
options.D: Medical knowledge and technology constantly advance

explanation: So true! Healthcare changes every day, so ongoing learning helps us give the safest, most modern care possible. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which official body regulates nursing practice and education right here in Nigeria?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: Well done! The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN) is the main body guiding our profession. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why is it so important for you as a student to know your legal scope of practice?

options.A: To replace doctors during major surgeries
options.B: To provide safe care within legal boundaries
options.C: To negotiate hospital budgets and salaries
options.D: To avoid paying professional association dues

explanation: Spot on! Knowing your boundaries keeps you legally safe and ensures your patients get the proper care they deserve. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h7)
